ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the battery and ammeter are on the left side, and after the current passes through the upper wire it first passes through a 20Ω resistor. An upper node is formed on the right side of the 20Ω resistor; from this node a 15Ω resistor is connected downward. The same upper node also continues rightward to connect to the upper end of the 30Ω resistor. Below is a return line; the lower end of the 15Ω resistor is directly connected to the lower wire. The lower end of the 30Ω resistor is connected through switch S to the same lower return line. Reasoning: When the switch is closed, the lower end of the 30Ω resistor is also connected to the lower return line, therefore the 15Ω resistor and the 30Ω resistor are both connected between the same two nodes: their upper ends are both connected to the upper node after the 20Ω resistor, and their lower ends are both connected to the lower return line. Components connected between the same two nodes are in parallel, and the potential difference across parallel components is equal. Therefore, the potential difference across the 15Ω resistor is equal to the potential difference across the 30Ω resistor.
